source_passages.quote:
For many applications at laboratory scale, contaminant molecules are not always a significant problem. Affinity 
chromatography (AC) will provide sufficient purity and, as long as the presence of any minor contaminants does not 
interfere with the intended application, the purified sample can be used directly.
source_passages.scope: Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
Common contaminants after initial purification are albumin, transferrin, antibody aggregates, leached protein A, DNA, 
and host or bovine immunoglobulins that originate from ascites or cell culture serum. The problem of contaminants of 
animal origin in, for example, bovine cell culture systems for monoclonal antibody (MAb) production, has been largely 
circumvented by use of serum-free systems. The three main contaminants albumin, transferrin, and host or bovine 
immunoglobulins pose three different purification problems: albumin because of its abundance; transferrin because of its 
similarity to the charge characteristics of many antibodies; and host or bovine immunoglobulins because of the similarity 
to that of the target immunoglobulin.
source_passages.scope: Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
Select chromatography techniques that utilize differences in the characteristics of the contaminant and target 
molecule: ion exchange chromatography (IEX) for separation by differences in charge; hydrophobic interaction 
chromatography (HIC) for separation by differences in hydrophobicity; and size exclusion chromatography (SEC) for 
separation by size. See Appendix 9 for an overview of the principles of the chromatography techniques used  
at laboratory scale.
source_passages.scope: Contaminants after initial antibody purification; laboratory-scale guidance
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote: Bovine immunoglobulins
source_passages.scope: Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
Co-purification of host or bovine immunoglobulins is a problem associated with any affinity purification of antibodies 
from a native source or a source to which supplements such as calf serum or bovine serum albumin are added. This 
contamination problem has been largely circumvented in the large-scale manufacture of MAbs for therapeutic use 
through the widespread use of serum-free cell culture systems.
source_passages.scope: Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
Difficulties have also been encountered when murine monoclonal antibodies are the target molecule. The similarities 
between the physical characteristics of the target antibody and the contaminants require careful selection and 
optimization to find the most suitable chromatography technique for purification. Both HIC and IEX can be used.
source_passages.scope: Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
The hydrophobicity of proteins is difficult to predict. Screen several chromatography media with different 
hydrophobicities (e.g., using HiTrap HIC Selection Kit) to find the medium that gives optimal results.
source_passages.scope: Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
HiTrap HIC Selection Kit includes seven HIC media with different hydrophobic properties for small-scale screening and 
selection of optimal binding and elution conditions. Figure 4.1 shows an example of chromatography media screening 
of a mouse monoclonal antibody on different HIC media prepacked in HiTrap 1 mL columns. In this case, the optimal 
medium for purification was HiTrap Phenyl HP.
source_passages.scope: Host or bovine immunoglobulin co-purification
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote: Albumin and transferrin
source_passages.scope: Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
Ion exchange and hydrophobic interaction chromatography are two methods used for removing albumin and transferrin, 
separating the molecules on the basis of differences in their isoelectric points or hydrophobicities (see Appendix 9 for the 
principles of these techniques).
source_passages.scope: Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
After an IEX purification, albumin and transferrin can be present if their charge properties are similar to those of 
the target antibody. In some cases, it might be possible to optimize pH and elution conditions in the IEX step to 
improve the separation between the antibody and the contaminants (Appendix 9).
source_passages.scope: Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
Since most monoclonal antibodies are more hydrophobic than albumin and transferrin, HIC can be used to bind the 
antibody and allow these contaminants to wash through the column.
source_passages.scope: Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote: However, AC using Blue Sepharose 6 Fast Flow is a useful alternative to IEX and HIC for removing albumin.
source_passages.scope: Albumin and transferrin after antibody purification
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote: Removal of albumin using Blue Sepharose chromatography media
source_passages.scope: Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
Blue Sepharose 6 Fast Flow or prepacked HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL columns (Fig 4.2) can be used to remove albumin 
either before or after other purification steps (see Table 4.1). The albumin binds in a nonspecific manner by electrostatic 
and/or hydrophobic interactions with the aromatic anionic ligand, Cibacron Blue F3G-A, coupled to Sepharose.
source_passages.scope: Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
Use HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL or 5 mL columns to remove host albumin from mammalian expression systems or when 
the sample is known to contain high levels of albumin that might mask the UV absorption of other protein peaks.
source_passages.scope: Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
Do not use Blue Sepharose chromatography media if the immunoglobulin or other target molecule has a 
hydrophobicity similar to that of albumin.
source_passages.scope: Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote: The protocol for removal of albumin using HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL columns is described below.
source_passages.scope: Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote: Albumin removal
source_passages.scope: Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
5. Apply the sample using a syringe fitted to the Luer connector or by pumping it onto the column. For optimal 
results, use a flow rate of 0.2 to 1 mL/min (1 mL column) and 0.5 to 5 mL/min (5 mL column) during sample 
application*.
source_passages.scope: Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
6. Wash with binding buffer (generally at least 5 to 10 column volumes) until the absorbance reaches a steady 
baseline or no material remains in the effluent. Maintain a flow rate of 1 to 2 mL/min (1 mL column) and  
5 to 10 mL/min (5 mL column) for washing.
source_passages.scope: Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
7. Elute with elution buffer using a one-step or linear gradient. For step elution, 5 column volumes is usually 
sufficient. For linear gradient elution, 10 to 20  column volumes are usually sufficient. Maintain a flow rate of  
1 to 2 mL/min (1 mL column) and 5 to 10 mL/min (5 mL column) for elution.
source_passages.scope: Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

source_passages.quote:
*       1 mL/min corresponds to approximately 30 drops/min when using a syringe with a 1 mL HiTrap column; 5 mL/min corresponds to approximately 
120 drops/min when using a 5 mL HiTrap column
source_passages.scope: Albumin removal using Blue Sepharose / HiTrap Blue HP 1 mL and 5 mL
source_passages.association_basis: Assistant visual check of Poppler rendering; pending human review

references.expected_answer: The sample can be used directly as long as minor contaminants do not interfere with the intended application; this is conditional laboratory-scale guidance.
reservations: No guaranteed absence of contaminants.
No universal requirement or prohibition of another purification step.

references.expected_answer: The text cites albumin abundance, transferrin charge similarity to many antibodies and host/bovine immunoglobulin similarity to the target. IEX, HIC and SEC exploit charge, hydrophobicity and size differences respectively; no medium is selected for this sample.
reservations: No diagnosed contaminant or guaranteed separation.
Separate general principles from an operating recipe.
references.novelty_limit: New comparison of the three stated difficulties.

references.expected_answer: The contamination problem has been largely circumvented in large-scale therapeutic MAb manufacture, not universally eliminated. Similar physical characteristics motivate careful selection and optimization; both HIC and IEX can be used.
reservations: Retain largely and the large-scale therapeutic-manufacture scope.
No claim that every serum-free sample is contaminated or contaminant-free.
references.novelty_limit: New limit on a source-context statement; shared bovine family.

references.expected_answer: Seven media with different hydrophobic properties support small-scale screening and selection of binding/elution conditions. Phenyl HP was optimal in the illustrated case. No seven-column series or transferable operating conditions are specified.
reservations: Seven media are not seven mandatory steps.
No medium selection or operating numbers inferred from the example.
references.novelty_limit: New interpretation of the seven-media example.

references.expected_answer: Similar charge properties can leave contaminants after IEX; in some cases pH and elution conditions may be optimized. Most monoclonal antibodies are more hydrophobic than albumin/transferrin, allowing HIC to bind antibody while contaminants wash through. Switching is not required in every case.
reservations: No exact pH or automatic adjustment rule.
Retain in some cases and most; no applicability guarantee.
references.novelty_limit: New joint comparison; substantial known-fact overlap.

references.expected_answer: Albumin removal with the named Blue products can occur before or after other purification steps. The warning against use when the target has hydrophobicity similar to albumin still applies.
reservations: No universal selectivity claim.
Ordering flexibility does not cancel the warning.

references.expected_answer: For a 1 mL column, loading uses 0.2–1 mL/min; washing uses 1–2 mL/min, generally at least 5–10 column volumes until steady baseline or no material remains. Approximately 30 drops/min corresponds to 1 mL/min using a syringe with a 1 mL HiTrap column; this is not an exact universal syringe conversion.
reservations: Separate loading and washing; preserve the endpoint and generally.
Keep approximate and column/syringe scope; no calculated duration.
references.novelty_limit: New loading misuse and approximate drop-rate question; overlaps C07.

references.expected_answer: Step elution usually needs 5 column volumes; a linear gradient usually needs 10–20. Elution flow for the 5 mL column is 5–10 mL/min. No single fixed duration is prescribed; do not invent one or transfer the 1 mL flow range.
reservations: Retain usually sufficient rather than guaranteed.
No calculated timing or complete albumin-removal guarantee.
references.novelty_limit: New size/step/volume combination; shares established facts.

references.expected_answer: Clarify the intended application/interference, contaminant information and differences from the target relevant to technique choice. Examples and general separation principles do not identify the signal or select a procedure.
reservations: No presumed deposit, contaminant identity or selected technique.
Do not require a confirmed diagnosis before asking for useful context.
references.novelty_limit: New underspecified request omits technique names; known-source challenge.

references.expected_answer: The protocol scope is located, but the equilibration excerpt E121-EQ has not been individually validated and is excluded. Withhold equilibration numbers pending review; loading/washing settings do not substitute for them. This is a corpus-eligibility limit, not absence from the manual.
reservations: Never promote E121-EQ or E118-I to approved status.
No equilibration quantities/flows from pending evidence or another step.
references.novelty_limit: New eligibility boundary; forbidden evidence is not required as retrievable.
